courses.title: Deep Learning
outcomes: Describe the fundamental concepts of neural networks and optimization techniques.
Apply Convolutional Neural Networks and their architectures for image classification and object
Analyze Vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU models for sequence modeling.
Design Autoencoders and Generative Adversarial Networks for real-world applications.
Evaluate transfer learning methodologies using pre-trained models.
Demonstrate the construction of neural networks from scratch.
Apply Convolutional Neural Networks for image classification.
Examine the performance and gradient behavior of Vanilla RNN, LSTM and GRU for sequence
Design Autoencoders and Generative Adversarial Networks for image reconstruction and generation
Evaluate transfer learning strategies using pre-trained models.

units.title: UNIT-I
units.content: Introduction: What is Deep Learning, Relationship between AI, ML and DL, Biological Neuron and Artificial Neuron, Perceptron - McCulloch-Pitts Model, Limitations of Perceptron, Layers, Multi-Layer Perceptron, Activation Functions, Forward pass, Backward pass, Loss Functions, Optimizers, Vanishing and Exploding Gradient Problems, Regularization - L1, L2, Dropout.

units.title: UNIT-II

units.title: UNIT-III
units.content: RNN: Vanilla RNN - Architecture and Limitations, Vanishing Gradient in RNNs, Bidirectional RNNs, LSTM - Cell State, Gates (Input, Forget, Output), GRU - Architecture and Comparison with LSTM.

units.title: UNIT-IV
units.content: Autoencoders: Introduction to Autoencoders - Encoder, Bottleneck, Decoder, Undercomplete Autoencoders, Denoising Autoencoders, Variational Autoencoders (VAE), Generative Adversarial Networks(GAN).

units.title: UNIT-V
units.content: Transfer Learning - Introduction and Motivation, When to use Transfer Learning - small dataset scenarios, similar vs dissimilar domains, Feature Extraction vs Fine-Tuning, Selective Layer Freezing strategies, Challenges - Negative Transfer, Domain Shift.

labExperiments: Week 1: Implement a Neural Network from scratch using only NumPy - build forward pass, backward pass and gradient descent without any deep learning framework and train on a binary classification dataset to verify correctness.

Week 2: Compare activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, LeakyReLU), weight initialization strategies (Random, Xavier, He) and regularization techniques (Dropout, L2) by training MLPs on MNIST and visualizing their effect on training loss and accuracy.

Week 3: Build a Multi-Layer Perceptron using PyTorch with a manual training loop, experiment with learning rate schedulers, momentum and batch normalization, plot training and validation loss curves to analyze convergence behavior.

Week 4: Implement a Convolutional Neural Network for MNIST digit classification, compare it against a fully connected network in terms of accuracy, number of parameters and training time, visualize learned filters and feature maps.

Week 5: Build a CNN for CIFAR-10 image classification, experiment with different architectures varying depth, filter sizes and pooling strategies, apply data augmentation techniques to improve generalization.

Week 6: Apply a pre-trained CNN (VGG16 or ResNet50) for a custom image classification task using Keras, visualize intermediate layer activations and compare performance with and without data augmentation.
Week 7: Review and Skill Test-1

Week 8: Implement Vanilla RNN, LSTM and GRU for sentiment analysis on the IMDB dataset, compare classification accuracy, training time and gradient behavior, visualize the vanishing gradient problem in Vanilla RNN.
Week 9: Build a character-level language model using LSTM for text generation, train on a custom text corpus and generate new text sequences by sampling from the learned probability distribution.

Week 10: Implement a Denoising Autoencoder and a Variational Autoencoder on MNIST, compare reconstruction quality on noisy inputs, and visualize the 2D latent space to analyze how the model organizes digit representations.

Week 11: Implement a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate handwritten digits, plot generator and discriminator loss curves during training, visualize the progression of generated image quality across epochs.

Week 12: Apply transfer learning using ResNet50 pre-trained on ImageNet for a small custom image dataset, compare three strategies - feature extraction with frozen layers, fine-tuning top layers and full fine-tuning - in terms of accuracy and training time.

Week 13-14: Build an end-to-end transfer learning pipeline for a real-world multi-class classification problem such as medical imaging or plant disease detection, evaluate using precision, recall and F1 score, deploy the model as a web application using Gradio.
Week 15: Review and Skill Test-2

labExperiments: Week 1: Explore and compare BPE, WordPiece and SentencePiece tokenizers across BERT, GPT-2 and LLaMA using HuggingFace Tokenizers library by analyzing vocabulary sizes, token counts and tokenization behavior on sample sentences, and run a pre-trained LLM locally for the first time using Ollama.
